title: Research
text:
Refereed Publications

Jacobson, T. (2025), “Strong Oracle Guarantees for Partial Penalized Tests of High Dimensional Generalized Linear Models,” Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B, DOI: 10.1093/jrsssb/qkaf010.
Jacobson, T. and Zou, H. (2025), “Linear Hypothesis Testing for High Dimensional Tobit Models,” Statistica Sinica, DOI: 10.5705/ss.202023.0118
Jacobson, T. Ding, J., and Zou, H. (2024), “Predicting 5G Throughput with BAMMO, a Boosted Additive Model for data with Missing Observations,” Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series C, 74(1), 249-273, DOI: 10.1093/jrsssc/qlae054.
Jacobson, T. and Zou, H. (2023), “High-Dimensional Censored Regression via the Penalized Tobit Likelihood,” Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 42(1), 286-297, DOI: 10.1080/07350015.2023.2182309
Anderson, L. and Jacobson, T. (2023), “Providing the choice of in-person or video-conference attendance in a Clinical Physiology course may harm learning outcomes for the entire cohort,” Advances in Physiology Education, DOI: 10.1152/advan.00160.2022
Jacobson, T. & Zou, H. (2021), “Do Predictor Envelopes Really Reduce Dimension?” Journal of Data Science, 4, 528-541. DOI: 10.6339/21-JDS1017



Preprints

Jacobson, T. (2025) “Nonparametric Envelopes for Flexible Response Reduction.” arXiv: 2509.07248
Jacobson, T. and Kwon, O. (2025) “Envelope-Guided Regularization for Improved Prediction in High Dimensional Multivariate Regression.” arXiv: 2501.11791



Software

Jacobson T. (2022). tobitnet: Penalized Tobit Regression. R package version 1.0.0, https://github.com/TateJacobson/tobitnet
Jacobson T. (2023). TobitTest: Linear Hypothesis Testing for High Dimensional Tobit Models. R package version 1.0, https://github.com/TateJacobson/TobitTest

title: Tate Jacobson
text:
I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics at Oregon State University. I completed my PhD in Statistics at the University of Minnesota where I worked with Professor Hui Zou. My research is mainly focused on developing new methods for analyzing high-dimensional data, though I am also interested in machine learning more broadly.





High-dimensional estimation and inference
Nonparametric and semi-parametric methods
Missing and censored data
Dimension reduction
Machine learning






PhD in Statistics, 2023
University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN
BA in Mathematics, 2016
Whitman College, Walla Walla, WA
